title: The pawn, promotion and en passant

card.idea: A pawn walks forward one square, or two on its very first move, and it never goes back. It takes differently from the way it walks: one square diagonally forward. Reach the far end of the board and the pawn turns into a piece of your choosing.

explain.text: Forward one square. On its first move a pawn may go two instead, which is why this one can reach e3 or e4. It can never move backwards and it can never step onto an occupied square.
Walking and taking are two different moves. Straight ahead to e5 if the square is empty, or diagonally onto d5 or f5 to take. A pawn can never take the piece directly in front of it.
Black has just pushed two squares past your pawn. On this move only, you may take it as if it had gone one square: your pawn lands on d6 and theirs comes off. This is called en passant.

challenges.prompt: Tap every square the pawn can move to.
challenges.reason: One square, or two because this pawn has not moved yet.

challenges.prompt: Tap every square the pawn can move to.
challenges.reason: Straight ahead to e5, or diagonally to take either pawn.

challenges.prompt: Tap the square where this pawn becomes a queen.
challenges.reason: One step to the eighth rank and the pawn is a pawn no longer.

wrong.e8=R+: A rook works, but you were offered a queen and turned it down.
wrong.h3: The pawn is one square from the end. Take the queen.

challenges.reason: A pawn on the last rank becomes whatever you ask for, so ask for the queen.

challenges.prompt: Black has just played d7-d5. Take that pawn.

wrong.e6: Walking past it. The two-square push can be answered right now, and only right now.
wrong.Ra5: The rook is not the piece with the offer on the table.

challenges.reason: En passant: your pawn lands on d6 and the pawn that ran past comes off.

wrong.exf6: That wins the bishop. The rook on the other side is worth more.
wrong.e6: Straight ahead takes nothing at all.

challenges.reason: Both are free, and a rook beats a bishop.

challenges.prompt: Win as much as you can with the pawn.

wrong.dxc6: The bishop, when a rook was on offer on the other diagonal.
wrong.d6: Pushing forward wins nothing and the pawn is then stuck.

challenges.reason: One little pawn, two things to take, so take the rook.

challenges.prompt: Take and promote in the same move.

wrong.b8=Q+: That makes a queen but leaves theirs on the board. Take it on the way.
wrong.bxa8=R+: You took the queen and then asked for a rook.

challenges.reason: The pawn takes diagonally onto the last rank, so it takes and promotes at once.

takeaway: Pawns walk straight, take diagonally, and become a queen at the end.
